title: Conjecture 7.1
statement_text: For every $t$, there is an output-polynomial time algorithm for Dom-Enum in incomparability graphs of $S_{t}$-free posets.
context_text: Dom-Enum is the problem of listing all (inclusion-wise) minimal dominating sets of a graph $G$; since there may be exponentially many, an algorithm is output-polynomial if its running time is polynomial in the size of the input plus the number of minimal dominating sets output. Whether Dom-Enum (equivalently, enumeration of the minimal transversals of a hypergraph) admits an output-polynomial algorithm is a long-standing open question, and it is as hard in co-bipartite graphs (complements of bipartite graphs) as in general. The comparability graph of a poset $P$ has an edge between any two comparable elements, its incomparability graph an edge between any two incomparable elements; co-bipartite graphs are incomparability graphs, so Dom-Enum in incomparability graphs is as hard as in general. The dimension of $P$ is the least $d$ such that $P$ is the intersection of $d$ linear orders, and the standard example $S_t$ is the poset on $a_1,\dots,a_t,b_1,\dots,b_t$ with $a_i<b_j$ exactly when $i\ne j$; $S_t$ has dimension $t$, so posets of dimension less than $t$ are $S_t$-free (contain no $S_t$ as an induced suborder), but some $S_t$-free posets have unbounded dimension. The authors give a polynomial-delay algorithm for Dom-Enum in incomparability graphs of posets of bounded dimension (given with the $d$ linear orders) and an incremental-polynomial algorithm in comparability graphs of posets of bounded dimension, the latter actually covering comparability graphs of all $S_t$-free posets. The conjecture asks for the counterpart in incomparability graphs; the authors' proof does not extend naturally since it relies on the bounded-dimension geometric representation, but they believe an extension is possible with different tools. An easier conjecture is the case of $2K_p$-free incomparability graphs ($2K_p$ being two disjoint $p$-cliques), since an $S_{2p}$ suborder yields a $2K_p$ in the incomparability graph; it holds for $p\le2$.
paper_title: Enumerating minimal dominating sets in the (in)comparability graphs of bounded dimension posets

title: Conjecture 7.2
statement_text: For every $p$, there is an output-polynomial time algorithm for Dom-Enum in $2K_{p}$-free incomparability graphs.
context_text: This is described as a directly easier version of Conjecture 7.1: an $S_{2p}$ suborder in a poset yields a $2K_p$ in the incomparability graph, so Conjecture 7.2 would follow from 7.1. It holds trivially for $p=1$ (such graphs are cliques) and is true for $p=2$ via results of [bonamy2020kt]; the case $p=3$ is widely open even without the incomparability assumption.
paper_title: Enumerating minimal dominating sets in the (in)comparability graphs of bounded dimension posets

title: Conjecture 7.3
statement_text: For any co-bipartite $H$, there is an output-polynomial time algorithm for Dom-Enum in $H$-free incomparability graphs.
context_text: Dom-Enum is the problem of listing all (inclusion-wise) minimal dominating sets of a graph $G$; since there may be exponentially many, an algorithm is output-polynomial if its running time is polynomial in the size of the input plus the number of minimal dominating sets output. Whether Dom-Enum (equivalently, enumeration of the minimal transversals of a hypergraph) admits an output-polynomial algorithm is a long-standing open question, and it is as hard in co-bipartite graphs (complements of bipartite graphs) as in general. The comparability graph of a poset $P$ has an edge between any two comparable elements, its incomparability graph an edge between any two incomparable elements; co-bipartite graphs are incomparability graphs, so Dom-Enum in incomparability graphs is as hard as in general. The dimension of $P$ is the least $d$ such that $P$ is the intersection of $d$ linear orders, and the standard example $S_t$ is the poset on $a_1,\dots,a_t,b_1,\dots,b_t$ with $a_i<b_j$ exactly when $i\ne j$; $S_t$ has dimension $t$, so posets of dimension less than $t$ are $S_t$-free (contain no $S_t$ as an induced suborder), but some $S_t$-free posets have unbounded dimension. The authors give a polynomial-delay algorithm for Dom-Enum in incomparability graphs of posets of bounded dimension (given with the $d$ linear orders) and an incremental-polynomial algorithm in comparability graphs of posets of bounded dimension, the latter actually covering comparability graphs of all $S_t$-free posets. Since co-bipartite graphs are incomparability graphs and Dom-Enum is hard on them, the question for $H$-free incomparability graphs is only interesting for co-bipartite $H$. Known cases: $H=K_p$ (bounded clique number, i.e. posets of bounded width) is covered by earlier work of Bonamy, Defrain, Heinrich, Pilipczuk and Raymond; $2K_p$-free incomparability graphs are solved for $p\le2$ and conjectured for all $p$, the case $p=3$ being widely open in general graphs; $C_4$-free incomparability graphs are interval graphs, where linear delay is known, while $C_4$ is the smallest open case for general graphs. Rather than debating natural generalizations (two cliques joined by a matching, a clique minus a matching), the authors state this bold conjecture, and remark that there is no blatant reason why the incomparability condition would be necessary.
paper_title: Enumerating minimal dominating sets in the (in)comparability graphs of bounded dimension posets
